title: Maria Klobenstein Pilgrimage Church Kössen
name: Maria Klobenstein Pilgrimage Church Kössen
kurzbeschreibung: Maria Klobenstein in the Entenlochklamm gorge near Kössen: ancient place of worship at the split rock ('Klobenstein') with a Baroque pilgrimage chapel and suspension bridge.
beschreibung:
Overview

The myth-enshrouded pilgrimage site of Maria Klobenstein is nestled in the wild and romantic Entenlochklamm gorge near the Tyrolean municipality of Kössen in the Kaiserwinkl (Bezirk Kufstein) at an elevation of approximately 560 metres. Situated right on the Bavarian-Tyrolean border along the Großache river, this fascinating ensemble is distinguished by its location next to a gigantic, split rock boulder – known as the “Geklobener Stein”. For centuries, this site has ranked among the most mysterious spiritual places of power in the Tiroler Unterland, magically drawing pilgrims, hikers, and nature lovers alike.

Miracle Rock, Pilgrimage & Suspension Bridge

According to legend, in the year 1711 a poor peasant woman encountered a devastating mudslide on her way to Kössen. In mortal fear, she prayed to the Virgin Mary for assistance, whereupon the hurtling boulder miraculously split in two ("klobte"), providing her with safe shelter between the towering rock faces. Out of heartfelt gratitude, a Baroque votive chapel was built directly into the rock fissure. To this day, pilgrims and visitors walk through the narrow cleft, which folklore credits with healing and purifying energies. The Baroque pilgrimage church captivates visitors with its artistic high altar and numerous historic votive tablets. In recent years, the sacred site has been made accessible via the spectacular Schmugglerweg trail featuring two daring suspension bridges spanning the roaring rapids of the Entenlochklamm gorge.

Visit & Getting There

The outdoor grounds, the split rock, and the suspension bridges are accessible year-round and free of charge; the pilgrimage chapel is open during the daytime for prayer and visits. The adjacent historic Gasthaus Klobenstein serves traditional Tyrolean culinary specialities. Getting there by car: take the B172 from Kössen heading towards Schleching (D), directly at the border lies the free Klobenstein hikers' car park. On foot: follow the signposted adventure trail Schmugglerweg from Kössen to reach the pilgrimage church in approximately one hour of walking. By public transport: regional buses run from Kufstein or St. Johann to Kössen.

Tips

Passing through the narrow rock crevice is an unforgettable adventure for both young and old; sturdy footwear is recommended for the natural trails in the gorge. Combine your outing with a scenic hike over the suspension bridges of the Schmugglerweg, taking in splendid views of the Rote Traun river and the Chiemgauer Alpen.
